Torch: NYU's new supercomputer. With over 500 Nvidia H200 GPUs, Torch is the most powerful supercomputer in American academic institutions. Torch is a perfect name: not only the emblem of NYU is a torch, but the software that primarily runs on Torch is PyTorch. (Py)Torch is intimately linked with NYU. FaceCrime: Fighting Image-Based Crime with Visual AI - NYC Visual AI Hackathon Project Our team built FaceCrime, a backend API designed to identify criminals by comparing uploaded images against a database of mugshots. Leveraging FastAPI, Jina AI CLIP, and a pgvector-powered Postgres database, we created a system that calculates image embeddings, performs similarity searches, and returns relevant metadata like offense and physical characteristics. ⚠️ Disclaimer: I was there for emotional support 😭, I BLINK and it took a minimum of 2 people to get an MVP up in a day Team: Gordon Ng , Malini R. , Eric Lin , Anthony Lamelas , Harrison Muchnic Key Features: - Facial Recognition API: Accepts image uploads or URLs and returns the closest matching mugshot from our database. - Jina AI CLIP Embeddings: Utilizes the Jina AI CLIP model for robust image embedding generation. - pgvector Similarity Search: Employs Postgres with pgvector for efficient and accurate similarity searches. - Dockerized Deployment: Easy deployment via Docker and Docker Compose. Built at the NYC Visual AI Hackathon hosted by Voxel51 and MongoDB. We had a fantastic time learning and collaborating with other ML enthusiasts. This project allowed us to explore the potential of Visual AI for real-world applications. Check out our project: - GitHub Repo (Backend): https://lnkd.in/et7_Htbg - GitHub Repo (Frontend): https://lnkd.in/epE6xKjR - Presentation Slides: https://lnkd.in/eTrYHAVD - Demo Site: https://facecrime.io/ #visualai #hackathon #machinelearning #facialrecognition #fastapi #jinaai #pgvector #docker #mongodb #voxel51 #python ...more ...more

As my Discovery II internship at Deloitte comes to a close, I want to take a moment to reflect on how grateful I am for this experience and everyone who helped make it so meaningful. Over the course of this internship, I had the opportunity to work with multiple public-company clients, supporting audit and reporting readiness work in preparation for filings. I supported the transition of documentation and reporting schedules, performed analytical procedures, and conducted audit testing across multiple areas. I also assisted in evaluating the materiality implications of a potential debt covenant breach, which provided valuable exposure to technical audit considerations and informed judgment in a dynamic, deadline-driven environment. This experience strengthened my technical skills, attention to detail, and ability to contribute across multiple engagements while balancing quality and deadlines. Most importantly, it deepened my appreciation for the collaboration and mentorship that make Deloitte such a special place to learn and grow. Thank you to Daniel Rodriguez , for being a great onboarding advisor, and to Brannon Watson, CPA , for your support and insight. Thank you as well to Anissa Ferrer for making the internship run smoothly and helping create such a meaningful experience. I’m truly grateful for this opportunity and excited to carry these lessons forward into what’s next.

Professor of Department of Computer Science & Engineering at NYU Tandon Justin Cappos spoke with Hadas Gold of CNN about an OpenAI model that escaped its test environment and broke into a real company’s servers when attempting to ace an internal cybersecurity evaluation last week: "The problem," Cappos said, "is that there’s a global race to dominate AI and make models that can improve themselves. Regulations could slow things down. So there’s a strong incentive for them to not have security controls unless their competitors also have those security and safety controls,” Cappos continues. “This is this is the fundamental dilemma.” #NYUTandonMade https://lnkd.in/e2ZG4Uxg

Detroit wasn’t what I expected. It wasn’t the city of decline that people often describe. From General Motors ’ modern Hudson headquarters in downtown Detroit to the peaceful lakes in Warren, this trip gave me a new perspective on both the city and the people driving the future of manufacturing. This week, I had the privilege of attending General Motors ’ 2026 Manufacturing Intern Day—and it also happened to be my very first business trip. Throughout the event, I had the opportunity to connect with fellow manufacturing interns from across North America, hear inspiring talks from General Motors ’ senior leadership, and gain valuable insights into the company’s vision, strategy, and commitment to innovation. It was exciting to see how every manufacturing site contributes to a much larger mission. I’m grateful for the opportunity to spend this summer as a Paint Controls/Process Engineering Intern at General Motors . Experiences like this remind me how much there is to learn, and I’m looking forward to continuing to grow both technically and professionally. Thank you to everyone who organized such an incredible event!
